steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Watercolour relies on the white of the paper for luminosity — work from light to dark, preserving highlights.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Acrylic is versatile: thin it for washes or apply thickly (impasto) for texture; it dries quickly so you can layer rapidly.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Wash techniques include flat wash (even tone), graded wash (light to dark), and wet-on-wet (blended, soft edges).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Glazing (thin transparent layers over dried paint) builds depth and richness in both watercolour and acrylic.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring working with watercolour and acrylic. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with working with watercolour and acrylic. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with working with watercolour and acrylic. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to working with watercolour and acrylic, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to ref | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
